description: Temporal plan validation checks a plan in which every action has a start time and, for a *durative action*, a duration. Each durative action splits into a start event and an end event. Events at the same time form a *happening*: its conditions are checked in the state before it, and then all its effects apply at once. Between happenings, fluents change linearly, and every `over all` condition of a running action must hold on the whole open interval; for linear change it is enough to check each condition at the roots of its comparisons and between them, so the check is exact. Two events that *interfere* (one changes what the other reads or changes) must be at least a small time ε apart, as PDDL 2.1 and the VAL validator require.

papers.title: PDDL2.1: An Extension to PDDL for Expressing Temporal Planning Domains

lineage.source: pddl-validate, src/validator/temporal.rs: "An untimed plan for a temporal task runs its steps at times 1, 2, 3, and so on"; the temporal timeline reuses the classical effect rule "apply all effects: deletes, adds, numeric updates"
